subject: Mid-year capacity true-up: discount phasing & invoice cutover
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — mid-year true-up questions

Hi Vivek,

We're starting our internal procurement review for our October renewal and I had a couple quick questions about how Redwood handles mid-year true-ups and phased discounts. Specifically:

- If we add capacity mid-contract, how are discounts applied? Is there a single blended discount or can we phase in a lower discount on the incremental capacity until we hit an annualized threshold?
- For invoicing, can we split a midterm add-on over two invoices to align with our fiscal cutover?

We're trying to model the economics for the board. Happy to hop on a short call — otherwise a written sketch is fine.

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Cloud Ops
Orbital Health

--
Attachment: procurement_window.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — mid-year true-up questions

Thanks for the clear questions, Elena — good timing to align before your procurement window. Short answers up front, then a recommended approach below.

1) Discount application on mid-contract add-ons:
- We do a blended approach by default for invoice simplicity, but we can also apply a two-tier structure: existing committed units keep the original band pricing; incremental units can be billed at a transitional discount for up to a quarter, after which they roll into the regular band if usage/commit thresholds are met.

2) Split invoicing for cutover:
- Yes — we can split the midterm add-on across two invoices to match your fiscal cutover. We call that an "invoice cutover" and it requires alignment on activation date and a short amendment.

Recommended path (what I propose now):
- Phase 1 (immediate add): Reserve incremental 25% capacity at a transitional 10% discount for 90 days.
- Phase 2 (validation): After 90 days, if usage justifies, convert the incremental capacity into the committed band and apply the standard renewal discount for the full term.
- Invoice: We provide invoice A for the prorated activation month and invoice B for the following month to complete the cutover.

I'm attaching a short proposal and a true-up worksheet that shows blended vs. phased pricing across likely usage scenarios. If that looks good I can draft the amendment language for legal and generate a DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
vivke@redwood.com

--
Attachments: Orbital_Renewal_Redwood_Proposal_v2.pdf (proposal stub); trueup_breakdown.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Elena Park <elena@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — mid-year true-up questions

Elena — quick follow-up with the finance mechanics so procurement has what they need.

- Transitional discount: We recommend the 10% transitional band be applied only to incremental reserved units, not to consumption overages. Consumption overages remain at standard pay-as-you-go rates.
- Proration example (from the attached worksheet): If you add 100 units on Aug 15, invoice A will charge pro-rated days (Aug 15–31) at the transitional rate; invoice B will include Sep 1–30 to complete the cutover.
- If you prefer a blended single-line credit instead, we can do that but it requires additional reconciliation at renewal.

Could procurement confirm whether they need a single PO covering both invoices or two separate POs? That will determine whether we keep a single amendment or two linked POs in our system.

-ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
